_voice: Polite gender-neutral "እርስዎ" forms (never the gendered አንተ/አንቺ), Ethiopic script.
_style: Address the user only with the polite gender-neutral እርስዎ forms (verbs ending -ዎ/-ዋል, e.g. «ያስቀምጡ», «ስምዎ», «ይፈልጋሉ?»); never use the gendered አንተ/አንቺ or their verb endings. For the couple together use «ሁለታችሁ» / «ሁለታችሁም» or the inclusive «አብረን», «የእኛ» (e.g. «የእኛ የአትክልት ስፍራ»). The other person is always «አጋርዎ» (your partner) — never ባል/ሚስት, ፍቅረኛዬ or gendered pronouns እሱ/እሷ; refer to the partner with the polite neutral «እሳቸው» or, better, repeat «አጋርዎ» or the name, and rephrase so no verb shows the partner's gender (prefer verbal nouns and passive/impersonal forms, e.g. «ደብዳቤ ተልኳል» instead of «ላከ/ላከች»). Messages one partner sends the other also use polite እርስዎ forms («እያሰብኩዎት ነው»). A partner's name placeholder (%@) is never declined or given prefixes/suffixes that would fuse with it (no የ%@, %@ን, ለ%@); rephrase instead, e.g. «አጋርዎ (%@)» or «%@ — …» or put the name as subject: «%@ ደብዳቤ ልከዋል». Quotes are guillemets « » (inner ‹ ›). Use Ethiopic punctuation: ። for sentence end, ፣ for comma, ፤ for semicolon, ፡ is not used between words (use normal spaces); ? and ! as in Latin, with no space before ? ! : ። ፣; keep the ellipsis “…”, “ · ” separators and \n exactly as in the source. Numbers stay in Western Arabic digits (1, 2, 3; never Ge'ez numerals), Gregorian dates as provided by the formatter, never convert to the Ethiopian calendar in text; write %lld before the noun («%lld ቀናት»). Ethiopic script has no case: keep brand names in Latin as-is (Coupley, Premium, CoupleSync, AI, iCloud), and keep buttons and tabs short — buttons use the polite imperative («ያስቀምጡ», «ይላኩ», «እንደገና ይሞክሩ») or a short noun, tabs are one or two words. Plural categories are ["one","other"]: one uses the singular noun («%lld ቀን»), other the plural («%lld ቀናት»). Tone: warm, light, kind, natural modern Addis Amharic — never flowery, never literal word-for-word.
